newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures open up, turn mixed.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures open up, turn mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures began mostly higher, but some soon cut their gains.

September Standard and Poor's 500 futures opened moderately higher amid buying by a dealer and a commission house, hitting a 942.00 session high. But buying faded and the market gave back most of those gains.
"Now we're trading back down -- it was just too overbought on the open," an S&P 500 trader said. He said trade was light.
One firm pegged fair value at 3.75 points premium to cash, buy programs at 5.50 points premium or wider and sell programs at 2.40 points premium or narrower.
"So far the whole thing has been hinged on the bonds," an S&P 500 futures trader said. "The bonds gave everything back early and so did we."
He said 934.00 to 935.00 had been a big support area in Sept S&Ps on Friday and was attracting buying early Monday.
Overall he called the market nervous.
"There's not much to trade off of today and we have bigger numbers later this week."
July retail sales and producer prices will be released on Wednesday, with consumer prices due Thursday.
Traders said that without firm T-bonds to prop up indicies, jitters from Friday's steep slide would continue.
September S&P 500 futures had fallen to a 2-1/2-week low on Friday as Treasury bonds and the dollar crumbled.
Early Monday, September T-bond futures peeked above 113-00, then turned lower again.
Traders pegged support for September S&Ps at 926.75, Friday's low, and at 917.00, the July 18 low.
Nikkei 225 futures were lower, continuing an overnight slide. September Nikkei fell below 19,000 and to the lowest price since late April.

At 0937 CDT/1437 GMT, September S&P 500s were up 0.85 point at 937.25, KCBT Value Lines were 1.00 higher at 836.50, new composites were 0.45 higher at 485.50, Midcap 400s were 0.15 higher at 312.90, Russell 2000s were down 0.50 at 414.00, and Nikkeis were 200 lower at 18,975.
